RAFAEL MORETTI-KLEIN
Principal Software Engineer | Backend Systems
Munich, Germany | rafael.morettiklein@example.com | +49 555 0505 505 | linkedin.com/in/rmk-example

SUMMARY
Backend engineer and engineering leader with 21 years of experience building large-scale services and distributed systems in Python, Go and C++. Technical experience includes API development, high-throughput service design, PostgreSQL and event-driven systems. Led organisations of up to 45 engineers and defined architecture for platforms serving 50M+ users; continue to write code every week, mostly internal tooling in recent years.

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Director of Engineering, Platform - Streamhaus GmbH (video streaming), Munich        2019 - Aug 2026
- Led the platform organisation: 5 teams, 45 engineers and 5 engineering managers, responsible for identity, playback API, billing integration and developer platform.
- Drove migration from a Python 2 monolith to approximately 60 Python and Go services on GKE; improved playback API availability from 99.5% to 99.95%.
- Reduced cloud spend by 31% (EUR 4.2M/year) through rightsizing, committed use discounts and an internal cost dashboard.
- Introduced an RFC process, architecture review board and on-call guidelines adopted company-wide.
- Grew the organisation from 18 to 45 engineers and conducted 200+ interviews.

Principal Engineer - Streamhaus GmbH                                                2015 - 2019
- Technical lead for the playback API, built with Python, Tornado and later an internal FastAPI-like framework, Cassandra and Redis.
- Designed an entitlement service handling 120k requests/second at peak using Go and Cassandra.
- Co-authored the company's service template and Python style guide.

Senior Software Engineer - Nordfels Telematik AG, Stuttgart                            2010 - 2015
- Developed backend systems for fleet telematics, ingesting GPS data from 300k vehicles using C++, Python, PostgreSQL/PostGIS and RabbitMQ.
- Led a team of 6 developers on the route-history product.

Software Engineer - Dataquelle Systems GmbH, Karlsruhe                               2005 - 2010
- Developed C++ and Python for industrial data acquisition software on Linux and embedded x86.
- Built a Python test harness used by QA for 8 years.

EDUCATION
Dipl.-Inf. (equivalent MSc) Computer Science, Rhine Valley University, 2005

SKILLS
Python (Django, Flask, FastAPI, Tornado, asyncio), Go, C++ (older); PostgreSQL/PostGIS, Cassandra, Redis, Kafka, RabbitMQ; GCP (GKE, Pub/Sub, BigQuery), AWS (EC2, S3), Kubernetes, Terraform; gRPC, Protobuf; Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry; distributed systems design, architecture reviews, technical hiring, people management

LANGUAGES
German (native), Italian (native), English (fluent)

PUBLICATIONS & TALKS
- “Running Python at 100k rps” - EuroPython-style conference talk, 2018
- “Cost is a feature” - internal platform engineering summit keynote, 2023

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, senior-level CV with a clear reverse-chronological structure, credible metrics, concise bullets, and substantial evidence of backend engineering and technical leadership. The strongest content includes the migration to approximately 60 services, 99.95% availability, 31% cost reduction, 120k requests/second entitlement service, and ingestion from 300k vehicles. The document is professional and readable. Its main content limitation is that several requirements are represented only indirectly: automated testing is mentioned through a test harness, but CI/CD is absent; PostgreSQL is listed, but query tuning and schema migrations are not; API development is evident, but REST API consumption is not explicit.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The headings, plain text layout, date formatting, and standard section order should parse well in ATS systems. Keyword coverage is strong for Python, Go, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Kafka, Kubernetes, Terraform, AWS, GCP, Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, distributed systems, and API work. AI/ATS screening probability is high for the general backend and Python requirements, but moderate rather than high for this specific vacancy because Docker, CI/CD, database migrations, query tuning, and explicit REST API consumption are not present. The CV should use the job's supported terminology more directly, especially automated testing, API design, architecture decisions, service reliability, and cloud deployment. Do not add Docker, CI/CD, query tuning, schema migrations, or REST consumption unless they are factually supported.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The candidate strongly exceeds the experience requirement and aligns well with Python backend services, high-throughput APIs, PostgreSQL, cloud deployment, event streaming, Kubernetes, Terraform, observability, technical trade-offs, and English communication. Fleet telematics and GPS ingestion provide relevant transport-domain adjacency, although the CV does not show freight forwarding, shipment tracking, carrier events, or EDI formats. Kafka, Kubernetes, Terraform, and observability are clear nice-to-have matches. The candidate's leadership background is considerably more senior than the advertised individual-contributor role, but the document usefully states that the candidate still writes code weekly. Candidate material does not establish Docker, query tuning, schema migrations, CI/CD, or Dutch/French; these are genuine gaps in the source information rather than defects that can be repaired through wording.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL / HIGH-VALUE ALIGNMENT IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Experience section under “Principal Engineer - Streamhaus GmbH,” change “Technical lead for the playback API, built with Python, Tornado and later an internal FastAPI-like framework, Cassandra and Redis” to “Designed and built a high-throughput playback API using Python, Tornado and an internal FastAPI-like framework, with Cassandra and Redis.” This makes the supported API-design experience more explicit without falsely claiming standard FastAPI or REST consumption.
2. In the Professional Experience section under “Senior Software Engineer - Nordfels Telematik AG,” change “Backend systems for fleet telematics: ingestion of GPS data from 300k vehicles...” to “Designed and maintained backend services for fleet telematics, ingesting GPS data from 300k vehicles using C++, Python, PostgreSQL/PostGIS and RabbitMQ.” This more directly matches backend services, event ingestion, and the job’s transport-domain context.
3. In the Professional Experience section under “Software Engineer - Dataquelle Systems GmbH,” change “Built a Python test harness used by QA for 8 years” to “Built an automated Python test harness used by QA for 8 years.” This uses the supported automated-testing terminology without claiming CI/CD.
4. In the Director of Engineering experience, change “Drove migration from a Python 2 monolith to approximately 60 Python and Go services on GKE” to “Drove migration from a Python 2 monolith to approximately 60 Python and Go backend services deployed on GKE.” This makes the supported cloud deployment experience more ATS-readable.
5. In the Summary, replace “Technical experience includes API development, high-throughput service design, PostgreSQL and event-driven systems” with “Technical experience includes Python backend services, API design, high-throughput service design, PostgreSQL, event-driven systems, and cloud deployment on GKE.” This improves alignment with the vacancy using only evidence already present in the CV.

MINOR ATS / PRESENTATION IMPROVEMENTS:
6. In the Skills section, group the existing skills under simple ATS-friendly labels rather than one long semicolon-separated line: “Languages & Frameworks,” “Databases & Messaging,” “Cloud & Infrastructure,” “Observability,” and “Architecture & Leadership.” Keep every technology currently listed; do not add Docker, CI/CD, database migrations, or query tuning.
7. In the Skills section, retain “AWS (EC2, S3)” but do not imply AWS deployment experience beyond what the source material supports. The experience section should continue to identify GKE as the documented deployment platform.
8. In the Summary, retain the statement that the candidate writes code every week, because it helps address the role’s hands-on expectations. Consider changing “mostly internal tooling in recent years” to “mostly internal tooling in recent years, following earlier hands-on ownership of Python APIs and high-throughput services” to connect that statement to the documented Principal Engineer work.
